Recharge is dominantly meteoric, followed by deep confined regional circulation toward the Black Sea drainage area.

research_enrichment.deposit_hydrogeological_context: Dobrinishte is a fracture thermal-water system in Paleozoic granites of the Rila-West Rhodope batholith. Recharge is predominantly meteoric through the higher parts of the massif, followed by deep circulation in a well-developed fracture system. The principal structural controls are NW-SE and NNW-SSE tectonic disturbances. The NW-SE fault system is thermowater-bearing and forms the main natural drainage pathway of deeply circulating fracture waters, while the oblique NNW-SSE faults partly barrier the thermal-water flow and promote ascending discharge at springs.

research_enrichment.deposit_hydrogeological_context: Guliyna Banya is a fracture-vein mineral-water system in the Razlog basin. Recharge occurs by infiltration of precipitation and/or river water along tectonic disturbance systems at depth. The collector is formed mainly by granites of the Central Pirin pluton and partly by gneisses of the Ograzhden lithotectonic unit. Natural drainage occurs along the Koneshtitsa and Pihla rivers; general groundwater-flow direction is SE-NW. Thermal springs occur in an arcuate zone approximately 850 x 200 m.

The collector is formed mainly by granites of the Central Pirin pluton and partly by gneisses of the Ograzhden lithotectonic unit. Natural drainage occurs along the Koneshtitsa and Pihla rivers; general groundwater-flow direction is SE-NW. Thermal springs occur in an arcuate zone approximately 850 x 200 m.

research_enrichment.geological_profile_note: The borehole crosses Neogene, Oligocene, Upper/Middle/Lower Eocene, Upper Cretaceous, Hotrivian and Malm-Valanginian strata. The official mineral-water identity is the Malm-Valanginian aquifer. The assessment also notes Middle Eocene limestones, sands and sandstones among permeable collector rocks encountered by the borehole; this is geological profile information, not a separate official mineral-water deposit assignment for R-68h.
research_enrichment.deposit_identity_note: FINAL OFFICIAL CORRECTION: MH assessment No.276/03.06.2024 is for R-68h Golden Sands and assigns it to Northeast Bulgaria Malm-Valanginian aquifer, Varna section. MH assessment No.278/03.06.2024 belongs to a different facility: C-5h Fabrika Hristo Botev, Varna Basin Eocene aquifer. R-68h is therefore not stored as a multi-aquifer official facility.
research_enrichment.source_correction_note: Current official MH register identifies No.278/03.06.2024 as C-5h Fabrika Hristo Botev, not R-68h. Previous MULTI_AQUIFER_OFFICIAL restoration was removed.
research_enrichment.deposit_hydrogeological_context: Official mineral-water facility in the pressurized fracture-karst Malm-Valanginian aquifer of Northeast Bulgaria, Varna section. The 1774 m borehole crosses younger strata, including Eocene units, before entering the deeper Malm-Valanginian carbonate collector. Crossing Eocene strata does not constitute a separate official Eocene mineral-water assignment for R-68h.
research_enrichment.deposit_fault_context: Regional fracture-karst carbonate system in the Varna monocline. Tectonic fracturing contributes to secondary permeability and deep groundwater circulation. No exact individual mapped-fault intersection is asserted for R-68h.
